    Bonds belong in the 401(k)

    In the brokerage, bond interest is taxed as ordinary income every single year. Inside the 401(k) it compounds untouched until you draw it.

    Holding the same 60 · 25 · 15 with bonds relocated saves roughly $400 a year in tax, for zero change in risk.

    Fourteen of those payment years land inside retirement. The plan’s income floor already carries every one of them, so this is a choice, not a problem.

    Pay it down, or invest?
    ASend an extra $500 a month to principal: debt-free about four years sooner, with ≈ $23K of interest never paid.
    BInvest that $500 a month instead: ≈ $114K at a 6% return by the same date, before tax.
    Slight edge: invest

    3.1% is a guaranteed return; markets are not. The spread favors investing, the certainty favors paying down. Either one is a good decision made on purpose.

    No other household debt. Nothing at card rates to clear first.

    Prototype notes

    Layout. No left rail on Home — top nav only, content across the full 1180px. Two independent flow columns, so a tall section never pads the one beside it: My Money and Strengthen my plan run down the left, My Plans and Get support down the right, with Your questions full-width below. Both second-row sections start around 900px, so they clear the fold on a full-height desktop window. Home page only — every other nav item, card link, and CTA is a dead link.

    Numbers. One persona (Marshall, 46, $620k net worth) with three plans — Baseline, Retire at 62, Go-Go Years. The plan scroller swaps the stat boxes, the retirement marker, and the projection curve together; everything else is static.

    Pin & rearrange. Hover a section header for two controls: pin holds it at the top of its column, and the grip drags it anywhere — either column, or the full-width band at the bottom, where it re-renders wide. The handle is also keyboard-operable (arrows move up, down, and between columns) and every move is announced to screen readers. A pinned section can cross columns but not be reordered inside one until it is unpinned. Order lives in memory only — a refresh restores the default, which is what "Reset layout" does too. Wiring it to saved user preferences is the real build.

    Today vs. planning. My Money is factual only — balances, this month's income and spending, a wellness read. The what-if sliders that used to live here are gone; scenario work belongs in My Plans or Optimize.

    Chart color. The treemap and allocation bar use a four-hue categorical set drawn from Boldin's palette (#0E8FA8, #FB5004, #0FA36F, #BC0278), validated for lightness band, chroma, colorblind separation, and 3:1 contrast against the card surface. Every block also carries a direct label, so identity never rests on color alone.

    Support card. Option 1 "Three Paths" content — same three tiers, same price pills — laid out as rows rather than tiles, because three photo tiles do not survive a 440px column. Photos are Unsplash placeholders in the brand's art direction; swap for licensed Boldin photography. Each falls back to a flat brand panel with the arch brandmark.

      Tax planning

      • The window
      • The ladder
      • The guardrail
      • Your move

      The next six years save you $61,000.

      Low-bracket years are rare. You are standing in two of them.

      The window

      $40K of low-bracket room, every year

      Between retiring in 2028 and RMDs at 75, your income drops and the 22% bracket sits half empty. Every unused dollar of that room expires each December 31.

      The conversion ladder

      Pay 22 cents now, never 25 later
      Convert $40,000 a year, 2026 to 2031
      $52,800 tax paid now
      12 to 22%
      Or leave it for RMDs at 75
      $113,800 tax paid later
      25%+
      The difference, kept by you
      $61,000 over the plan
      Yours

      Six quiet Decembers. Each conversion also shrinks future RMDs, which keeps Social Security less taxed and Medicare premiums lower. Smart compounds.

      The guardrail

      IRMAA at $212,000
      Your MAGI with conversions: $168,000Cliff: $212,000

      You clear the Medicare surcharge line by $44,000. The ladder is sized so you never trip it. Bold, with a seatbelt.

      Your move

      This December
      Convert $40,000 this December.
      Rung one of six. Twenty minutes with your custodian, and the cheapest tax rate of your retirement is locked in.
      Scheduled. Rung one is on the calendar.
      Six quiet Decembers

      Converting $40,000 a year through 2031 pays tax at 12 to 22 cents on the dollar instead of 25 and up. That is $61,000 kept, and smaller RMDs forever.

      Withdrawal strategy

      • The order
      • Guardrails
      • One month, mapped
      • Your move

      Paychecks by design for 31 years.

      Which dollars you spend first decides how long all of them last.

      The order

      Right sequence, longer money
      1 · Cash2028 to 2029
      2 · Taxable2029 to 2033
      3 · Tax-deferred2033 to 2050
      4 · Rothlast, untouched longest

      Taxable first keeps your brackets low while conversions run. The Roth compounds untouched the longest, which is exactly what tax-free money is for. Order alone adds about 2 years of portfolio life.

      Guardrails

      Raises in good years, never a guess

      Spending floats between $5,850 and $8,400: small raises after good markets, small trims after bad ones. The rule decides, so a headline never does.

      One month, mapped

      Where a $6,323 month comes from
      $3,180Social Security
      $1,420Pension
      $1,723Portfolio

      Two of these three arrive no matter what the market does. Only 27 cents of every dollar you spend ever depends on a good year.

        Release Notes

        What’s new in Boldin.

        We ship improvements every week. Here’s what’s changed lately.

        This week
        Jul 2026
        The Vision Board. Turn the life you’re planning for into something you can see, and price it against your plan on the spot. Find it on the Plan tab under Retirement.
        Jul 2026
        Inline editing. Update any account balance right where it sits, no dialog. Your net worth updates as you type.
        Jun 2026
        The Window. A new tax view maps the low-bracket years between your last paycheck and your first RMD, and shows what filling them is worth for life.
        Jun 2026
        Cash Flow, played forward. Slide through the years and watch your income and spending reshape as salaries give way to Social Security and portfolio draws.
        May 2026
        Boldin AI, full screen. Give the assistant room to work, with your chat history and a live infographic side by side.
        May 2026
        Faster account refreshes, a redesigned profile, and dozens of smaller fixes across the planner.

        Have an idea or found a bug? Tell us from the Help Center. A lot of what ships here starts as a member request.

        Your money, today

        TrueView

        82%complete

        TrueView is a snapshot of what is real right now. Every account, balance, and debt, exactly as it stands today. No projections, no assumptions, nothing imagined. Add more accounts and the view gets better. The future lives in your Plan; this is the ground it stands on.

        Your money, forward

        Your Plan

        87%confidence

        Your Plan is a forecast, not a statement. It takes what is true today and projects it forward from your inputs: when you retire, what you spend and save, and how your money grows. Change an input and the whole future redraws. Nothing here is a promise; it is the best current read of the road ahead.
